title: Artificial intelligence maturity in buyer–seller exchange
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping business-to-business (B2B) buying and selling, yet research has largely examined AI as a unilateral process enabler. While this perspective has generated important insights regarding AI adoption and performance, it overlooks a fundamental characteristic of B2B selling: exchange outcomes depend on the compatibility of buyer–seller decision processes at the exchange interface. To address this gap, the authors advance the concept of AI exchange maturity (i.e. extent to which decision authority within buyer–seller exchange is delegated to AI systems) and theorize its organizational antecedents. Building on this construct, the authors develop a bilateral theory of buyer–seller AI exchange in which value co-creation depends on the configuration of AI exchange maturity across exchange partners. The framework identifies four configurations (buyer AI-maturity advantage, seller AI-maturity advantage, agentic-AI maturity alignment, and pre-AI maturity alignment) and theorizes how each configuration shapes value co-creation through information-processing fit and buyer–seller trust. The authors further identify strategies for selling organizations to manage each configuration to enhance value co-creation. In doing so, the framework shifts the theoretical focus from whether individual firms adopt AI to the distribution of decision authority between humans and AI systems across exchange partners.

title: Star Light, Star Bright: Can Multimodal Models Parse an Astronomy Visual Question Answering Dataset Right?
abstract: Figures are essential for scientific communication, and the field of Visual Question Answering (VQA) aims to test the figure understanding capabilities of large multimodal models (LMMs). Here, we investigate the accuracy of several low-cost LMMs on domain-specific VQA tasks for astronomical images of the sky. As instrument for this task we build a domain-specific VQA dataset comprising 2001 partially-synthetic figures divided evenly between contour plots, real telescope images drawn from NASA's SkyView, and "fake" sky images which share the axes and angular scales of the real images but draw their colors from a gaussian mixture model, alongside 47357 questions. Each figure is released as pristine and with realistic page-aging degradations mimicking the historical astronomical corpus. Testing three low-cost proprietary LMMs, we find models frequently fail to answer domain-specific questions at high accuracy. An initial comparison with 104 human-verified, astrometrically tagged figures from historical journal publications shows similar median errors in angular extent. All code is available on GitHub: https://github.com/jnaiman/SkyImagesWASP2026 and dataset is available on HuggingFace: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ReadingTimeMachine/astro_sky_image_vqa.

title: X-RIC: An Agentic RAN-Intelligent Controller Benchmark for Enhancing Reinforcement Learning
abstract: The O-RAN ALLIANCE introduces architectural flexibility through disaggregation and AI-driven control. While the RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) enables centralized optimization, current AI approaches lack reasoning capabilities and explainability. We propose eXplainable RIC (X-RIC), a novel framework integrating agentic AI into O-RAN architectures. X-RIC combines reactive Reinforcement Learning (RL) with strategic agentic reasoning through: (i) automated Behavioral Cloning (BC) using domain heuristics for sample-efficient training, (ii) a Telecom Language Model (TLM), a transformer-based reasoning module providing contextual abstraction and interpretability, and (iii) closed-loop co-adaptation within the Near-RT RIC control loop enabling continuous policy refinement. To ensure deployment readiness, we introduce BARX (Benchmarking Agentic Reasoning for RAN), a domain-specific evaluation framework assessing agentic control across latency, compliance, and determinism metrics. We validate X-RIC on SLA-aware network slicing in simulation and O-RAN-compliant testbed deployments. X-RIC achieves 89% operational cost reduction while maintaining SLA compliance, converging 75% faster with 50% fewer training steps and 46% lower variance.

title: When Models Misread Ink: Auditing VLMs for Arabic Calligraphy Recognition
abstract: Arabic calligraphy is a high-stakes cultural visual domain for Muslim communities, yet VLM evaluations rarely test its fine-grained script traditions. We audit 12 VLMs on a cleaned 1,195-image six-way benchmark using numeric, visual-cue, and Diwani-first prompts. In this closed-set setting, the best numeric-prompt accuracy is 60.9% for closed/API models and 47.2% for open-weight models. The main failure is default-label collapse: every numeric run is dominated by a single label taking 33-63% of predictions, against an 18.8% majority-class baseline. For 8 of 12 models the default is Thuluth; GPT-4o labels 52.9% of all images as Thuluth although it is only 18.1% of the set. Prompting helps unevenly: visual cues move accuracy by more than 10 points for some models but hurt others, and foregrounding Diwani often relocates the default rather than removing it. Arabic calligraphy recognition is therefore a compact, culturally grounded stress test for VLM robustness and for measuring which visual traditions become legible to automated systems.

title: A study of cryptographic algorithms in the Internet of Things
abstract: Η ταχεία ανάπτυξη του Διαδικτύου των Πραγμάτων (Internet of Things - ΙοΤ) έχει οδηγήσει σε σημαντικές προόδους σε διάφορους κλάδους, συμπεριλαμβανομένων των κλάδων της υγείας, της βιομηχανίας, των μεταφορών και της γεωργίας. Έχοντας δισεκατομμύρια διασυνδεδεμένες συσκευές που παράγουν τεράστιο όγκο δεδομένων, υπάρχουν πολλές ευκαιρίες για καινοτομία και νέους αυτοματισμούς. Ωστόσο, νέες προκλήσεις ασφαλείας παρουσιάζονται συνεχώς. Όταν ευαίσθητες πληροφορίες μεταδίδονται μέσω μη ασφαλών διαύλων επικοινωνίας, οι συσκευές Διαδικτύου των Πραγμάτων γίνονται ελκυστικοί στόχοι για εγκληματίες του κυβερνοχώρου που επιδιώκουν να εκμεταλλευτούν γνωστές ευπάθειες ή αδυναμίες στα υπάρχοντα πρωτόκολλα ασφαλείας. Για να αντιμετωπίσουν αυτές οι ανησυχίες, οι ερευνητές έχουν στρέψει την προσοχή τους στην ανάπτυξη ισχυρών λύσεων κρυπτογράφησης προσαρμοσμένων ειδικά για περιβάλλοντα Διαδικτύου των Πραγμάτων. Οι λύσεις αυτές στοχεύουν να παρέχουν επαρκή προστασία χωρίς να διακυβεύονται οι περιορισμένοι διαθέσιμοι πόροι στις περισσότερες συσκευές IoT. Αυτή η εργασία στοχεύει να συμβάλει σε αυτό το συνεχώς αυξανόμενο σύνολο γνώσεων διερευνώντας το ρόλο των ελαφρών κρυπτογραφικών αλγορίθμων στην ενίσχυση της ασφάλειας του Διαδικτύου των Πραγμάτων. Ξεκινά παρέχοντας μια επισκόπηση, στην πρώτη ενότητα, σχετικά με το τι συνιστά ένα σύστημα Διαδικτύου των Πραγμάτων, επισημαίνοντας τα κύρια στοιχεία, τις αρχιτεκτονικές, τις εφαρμογές και τα οφέλη του. Στη δεύτερη ενότητα γίνεται εμβάθυνση στις μοναδικές προκλήσεις ασφαλείας που τίθενται από τις συσκευές Διαδικτύου των Πραγμάτων προτού ακολουθήσει συζήτηση για την σημασία της κρυπτογραφίας στην αντιμετώπιση αυτών των ζητημάτων. Συγκεκριμένα, αυτή η ενότητα θα εξηγήσει γιατί προτιμώνται οι ελαφρές τεχνικές κρυπτογράφησης έναντι των παραδοσιακών όταν ασχολούμαστε με συσκευές Διαδικτύου των Πραγμάτων με περιορισμένους πόρους. Στο σύνολο της εργασίας γίνεται ανασκόπηση της σχετικής βιβλιογραφίας και όπου αυτό είναι εφικτό θα συγκεντρώνονται εμπειρικά στοιχεία. Στο πλαίσιο της εμπειρικής αξιολόγησης πραγματοποιήθηκε software-based benchmarking των αλγορίθμων AES-128-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305 και ASCON-AEAD128 σε περιβάλλον Node.js. Για τις μετρήσεις χρησιμοποιήθηκαν δεδομένα από το Intel Lab Data, τα οποία διαμορφώθηκαν σε payloads μεγέθους 64, 256 και 1024 bytes, επιτρέποντας τη συγκριτική αξιολόγηση της απόδοσης των αλγορίθμων ως προς τους χρόνους κρυπτογράφησης και αποκρυπτογράφησης. Με την εξέταση διαφόρων ελαφρών κρυπτογραφικών αλγορίθμων και την αξιολόγηση της απόδοσής τους σε σενάρια του πραγματικού κόσμου, αυτή η εργασία επιδιώκει να εντοπίσει τους κατάλληλους αλγορίθμους κρυπτογράφησης για εφαρμογή στα οικοσυστήματα του Διαδικτύου των Πραγμάτων. Ο απώτερος σκοπός είναι η μεγιστοποίηση της ασφάλειας εξασφαλίζοντας ταυτόχρονα την ελάχιστη δυνατή επίδραση στην λειτουργικότητα των συσκευών καθώς και στην εμπειρία χρήσης.

title: A Deep Learning-Based Multi-Class Breast Cancer Histopathological Image Classification System Using CBAM
abstract: Breast histopathological image classification is challenging because benign and malignant breast lesions can exhibit overlapping cellular morphology, texture, staining appearance, and tissue architecture. This paper presents a multi-class deep learning framework that integrates the BreakHis dataset, ImageNet-pretrained InceptionResNetV2, and the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) for eight-class histopathological image classification. The pipeline performs class-distribution analysis, mean-count-based oversampling and undersampling, CLAHE-based contrast enhancement in LAB space, resizing to 224×224 pixels, normalization, and horizontal and vertical training augmentation. InceptionResNetV2 provides the main convolutional representation, while CBAM sequentially applies channel and spatial attention to refine discriminative feature information before a dense classification head. The latest ten-epoch training run reaches 98.44% training accuracy. The reported test evaluation achieves 98% accuracy on 2,160 test images, with 270 images per class. Macro precision, recall, and F1-score are approximately 0.98. The results demonstrate strong performance for the integrated pipeline under the reported benchmark protocol. evidence.title: A Deep Learning-Based Multi-Class Breast Cancer Histopathological Image Classification System Using CBAM
evidence.abstract: Breast histopathological image classification is challenging because benign and malignant breast lesions can exhibit overlapping cellular morphology, texture, staining appearance, and tissue architecture. This paper presents a multi-class deep learning framework that integrates the BreakHis dataset, ImageNet-pretrained InceptionResNetV2, and the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) for eight-class histopathological image classification. title: Exact Minimal Observable Realizations and Hankel Matrix Realization for Four-Qubit Lindblad Systems
abstract: This research announcement establishes the exact minimal observable realizations and underlying Hankel operator dimensions for an open four-qubit system governed by a finite-dimensional Lindblad master equation. We present complete numerical and algebraic validation showing that the minimal realization dimension (\(r_{\min }\)) undergoes a discrete structural transition between two distinct parameter values. Under exact rational arithmetic calculations evaluated over a finite field (\(\bmod\ 1,000,003\)), the system's output dynamics compress to a closed invariant subspace of exactly 21 dimensions at the baseline parameter state (\(a = 0.6\)), and expands to exactly 23 dimensions under a perturbed configuration (\(a = 0.601\)). This rank change rigorously indicates an exceptional parameter-space bifurcation. This post serves as an official time-stamped registration of these specific realization limits, verifying the exact dimensions of the observable manifolds prior to the publication of full derivation proofs and physical hardware tracking datasets.

title: IMOM G'AZZOLIY ASARLARI KORPUSINI SEMANTIK ANNOTATSIYALASH MODELI VA UNING LINGVISTIK IMKONIYATLARI
abstract: Annotatsiya. Mazkur maqolada Imom G‘azzoliy asarlarining o‘zbek tilidagi tarjimalari asosida shakllantirilgan elektron korpusni semantik annotatsiyalash modeli va uning lingvistik imkoniyatlari tadqiq etiladi. Tadqiqot materiali sifatida G‘azzoliyning o‘nta asaridan tuzilgan, taxminan 1,2 million belgidan, 200 ming token va 25 mingga yaqin unikal leksik birlikdan iborat korpusdan foydalanildi. Kalit so‘zlar: Imom G‘azzoliy, mualliflik korpusi, korpus lingvistikasi, semantik annotatsiya, semantik teglash, ontologiya, semantik maydon, semantik guruh, semantik klaster, WordNet, USAS, Sketch Engine. Аннотация. В данной статье исследуется модель семантического аннотирования электронного корпуса, сформированного на основе узбекских переводов произведений Имама аль-Газали, а также рассматриваются его лингвистические возможности. Материалом исследования послужил корпус, составленный на основе десяти произведений аль-Газали и включающий около 1,2 миллиона знаков, 200 тысяч токенов и почти 25 тысяч уникальных лексических единиц. Ключевые слова: Имам аль-Газали, авторский корпус, корпусная лингвистика, семантическая аннотация, семантическая разметка, онтология, семантическое поле, семантическая группа, семантический кластер, WordNet, USAS, Sketch Engine. Abstract. This article examines a semantic annotation model for an electronic corpus compiled from Uzbek translations of the works of Imam al-Ghazali, as well as its linguistic capabilities. The research material consists of a corpus compiled from ten works by al-Ghazali, comprising approximately 1.2 million characters, 200,000 tokens, and nearly 25,000 unique lexical units. Keywords: Imam al-Ghazali, authorial corpus, corpus linguistics, semantic annotation, semantic tagging, ontology, semantic field, semantic group, semantic cluster, WordNet, USAS, Sketch Engine.

title: AI-DRIVEN ONLINE ADAPTIVE LEARNING SYSTEMS IN HIGHER EDUCATION: AN INTEGRATIVE REVIEW OF LEARNER MODELLING, ADAPTATION MECHANISMS AND EVIDENCE OF EFFECTIVENESS
abstract: The rapid expansion of online and blended learning in higher education has exposed a persistent limitation of conventional online courses: content is delivered to all students in the same sequence and at the same pace, regardless of differences in prior knowledge, learning progress and needs. Online adaptive learning systems, increasingly powered by artificial intelligence (AI), aim to overcome this limitation by continuously diagnosing the learner and personalising content, sequence, difficulty and feedback. Aim. This article reviews the theoretical foundations, learner-modelling techniques, adaptation mechanisms and empirical evidence on the effectiveness of AI-driven online adaptive learning systems, and derives implications for higher education systems undergoing digital transformation, with particular reference to Uzbekistan. Methods. An integrative literature review was conducted following the framework of Whittemore and Knafl. Seminal works and peer-reviewed publications indexed in Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC and Google Scholar, together with international policy documents, were analysed using reflexive thematic synthesis. Results. Six themes were identified: (1) pedagogical and psychological foundations; (2) learner modelling, from Bayesian knowledge tracing to deep learning; (3) adaptation targets and mechanisms; (4) evidence of effectiveness from meta-analyses; (5) the emerging role of generative AI; and (6) ethical, pedagogical and infrastructural challenges. Meta-analytic evidence shows moderate to large positive effects of intelligent and adaptive tutoring on learning outcomes, while gaps remain regarding teacher involvement, transparency and applicability to low-resource language contexts. Conclusion. Effective adaptive learning requires the integration of validated learner models, pedagogically grounded adaptation rules, interoperable learning platforms and a teacher-in-the-loop approach. A set of requirements for national adaptive learning systems is proposed.

title: Confidence-Gated Prototype-Guided Graph Contrastive Learning for Semi-Supervised Encrypted Traffic Classification
abstract: Most existing encrypted-traffic classification methods treat each traffic flow as an independent sample, overlooking the relationships shared by similar flows. This can amplify within-class variation and increase overlap between classes, particularly when their distinguishing characteristics are subtle and labeled data are limited. To address this problem, we propose PGCL-CG, a prototype-guided semi-supervised graph contrastive learning framework. We represent flow-level statistical features as a sparse, weighted k-nearest-neighbor graph and use GraphSAGE to aggregate information from neighboring flows and to capture their underlying structural relationships. The encoder is pretrained using self-supervised graph contrastive learning to obtain stable representations. We use a student-teacher architecture to produce more stable pseudo-labels and apply hierarchical density-based spatial clustering to filter out low-confidence assignments. We conduct extensive experiments on the two open datasets, demonstrating that PGCL-CG outperforms competitive baselines and remains robust even when only a small fraction of labels (e.g., 20% or 40%) is available.

title: Optimizing corridor-type apartment floor layouts under regulatory constraints: a hybrid GA–SA–PSO and SWARA–CoCoSo approach
abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop a regulation-aware decision-support framework for optimizing corridor-type apartment floor layouts during the early planning and feasibility stage. The framework seeks to support developers and project managers in generating, evaluating and selecting feasible floor-layout alternatives while simultaneously satisfying selected encoded regulation-derived constraints, floor-efficiency targets and development objectives. Design/methodology/approach The study formulates corridor-type apartment-floor planning as a mixed discrete–continuous optimization problem under Vietnamese regulatory constraints. A hybrid optimization framework integrating genetic algorithm (GA), simulated annealing (SA) and particle swarm optimization (PSO) is developed to generate feasible layout alternatives. Regulatory requirements related to fire safety, circulation and geometric feasibility are embedded directly into the optimization process. Subsequently, the Step-Wise Weight Assessment Ratio Analysis (SWARA)–Combined Compromise Solution (CoCoSo) multi-criteria decision-making approach is employed to determine criterion weights and rank feasible alternatives according to stakeholder preferences. Three floorplate-capacity scenarios (Amax = 1,000, 1,400 and 1,800 m2) are examined through repeated computational experiments. Findings The proposed framework successfully generated feasible corridor-type apartment floor layouts that satisfied the selected encoded regulation-derived constraints and development-performance criteria. Results indicate that the 1,000 and 1,400 m2 scenarios achieved consistently high feasibility rates, whereas feasibility declined under the 1,800 m2 scenario because of increased design complexity and constraint interactions. For the representative 1,400 m2 scenario, five feasible alternatives were shortlisted for multi-criteria evaluation. The SWARA–CoCoSo analysis identified Layout A2 as the preferred solution under the baseline developer unit-mix target, reflecting the most favorable compromise among floor efficiency, premium-unit placement, accessibility to the vertical circulation core, floorplate utilization and unit-mix satisfaction. Sensitivity analysis further showed that the preferred alternative may change when the developer-defined product strategy is modified, with A3 becoming preferable under a more 1BR-oriented target. Originality/value This research contributes to the construction management and residential planning literature by proposing an integrated framework that combines regulation-aware layout generation, hybrid metaheuristic optimization and multi-criteria decision support within a single workflow. Unlike many existing studies that focus on identifying a single optimal solution or treat regulatory requirements as secondary considerations, the proposed framework embeds selected regulation-derived feasibility constraints directly into the search process and provides a portfolio of feasible alternatives for decision-making. The study offers a practical tool for supporting feasibility-stage planning and investment decision-making in high-rise residential developments.

title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
abstract: GPT-6-Astra demonstrates a level of competence in robotic manipulation and navigation that challenges the conventional paradigm of building specialized models for individual tasks and embodiments. In this report, we ask not only how capable GPT-6-Astra is, but what its capabilities imply for the field. First, we probe the limits of standalone GPT-6-Astra. We conduct a large-scale evaluation across 12 representative benchmarks spanning tabletop manipulation, humanoids, mobile platforms, and dexterous hands. Under a unified protocol that allows in-context learning (ICL) from training-set demonstrations and substantially increases the number of execution steps, GPT-6-Astra achieves unprecedented performance (Fig. 1). Future research may focus on improving 1) the generality of ICL 2) cost and execution time, 3) physical-state verification, 4) recovery from irreversible failures, and 5) long-horizon preservation of progress. Second, we study the agentic harness for embodied control. We identify that close-loop coordination between a high-level "System 2" reasoner (i.e., GPT-6-Astra) and a low-level "System 1" controller (e.g., π0.5) is costly but effective. Third, we examine GPT-6-Astra on real-world deployment. Our experiments on 8 robot configurations reveal substantial gaps: 1) robot demonstrations required for ICL are expensive to collect, and 2) it is implausible to trade longer execution for higher success rates with physical constraints. Fourth, we envision the next generation of embodied benchmarks. We develop a prototype that 1) derives tasks from real-world needs, 2) provides no in-domain demonstrations, and 3) judges agents on a world clock that keeps running while they deliberate. Taken together, our results suggest that GPT-6-Astra has largely crossed the threshold of embodied competence, but not yet that of practical embodied intelligence.

title: Beyond Pairwise Repulsion: Collective Diversity via Determinant Maximization in Diffusion Sampling
abstract: Strong guidance in text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models concentrates sampling toward high-density modes of the conditional distribution, collapsing independently sampled noise vectors onto nearly identical visual prototypes. This limits utility for tasks that demand distributional breadth, most critically synthetic data augmentation. Diversity, however, is a collective property of the whole batch: a set can preserve every pairwise distance yet still collapse onto a low-dimensional subspace. Existing sum-of-pairwise noise-optimization and repulsion objectives respond only weakly to this higher-order failure. We propose DetNO (Determinant Noise Optimization), which formulates diverse generation as RKHS volume maximization on the initial noise, maximizing the log-determinant of an RBF Gram matrix over one-step Tweedie predictions. This set-level functional equals the squared batch volume; its repulsion is strongest when the batch is most collapsed and self-attenuates as diversity is achieved. An anchor-based fidelity term keeps the optimized noises near plausible regions, and Lagrangian relaxation gives a two-term objective with a single hyperparameter $λ$ governing the diversity-quality trade-off, without training or sampler modification. Across three backbones (SD1.5, SDXL, SD3), DetNO achieves leading intra-batch diversity in VendiScore and Mean Self-Similarity, and a downstream few-shot classification experiment confirms that broader mode coverage brings statistically significant accuracy gains for synthetic data augmentation in the low-shot regime. Fixing the pipeline and varying only the batch objective, both RBF-based aggregators outperform InfoNCE, and the log-determinant attains the best downstream accuracy on both benchmarks. Its diversity advantage over InfoNCE widens as the batch grows. Code is available at https://github.com/mobled37/DetNO.

title: CARA: Causally Guided Retrieval Agent for Question Answering
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation over text-rich knowledge graphs requires identifying evidence that contributes to answering a question, rather than merely matching its textual content. Existing agentic retrievers adaptively balance global search and multi-hop exploration but primarily rely on textual similarity to guide retrieval. We propose CARA, a training-free, CAusally guided Retrieval Agent that explicitly evaluates the causal relevance of retrieved evidence through two complementary criteria: consequentiality, measuring whether adding evidence improves answerability, and essentiality, assessing whether removing evidence weakens answerability. CARA integrates these assessments with path consistency to guide graph exploration and employs reciprocal rank fusion to aggregate evidence from multiple agents. We evaluate CARA on three STaRK datasets and augment STaRK with ground-truth answers to enable downstream question answering evaluation. Experimental results demonstrate that CARA consistently outperforms existing retrievers. CARA also improves answer quality and faithfulness while examining fewer graph nodes and requiring fewer retrieval operations. These findings demonstrate that causal relevance assessment enables more focused and effective agentic graph retrieval, improving both retrieval performance and downstream question answering.

title: When Does "Post-Call" Begin? An Availability Contract for Earnings-Call NLP Benchmarks
abstract: Corporate financial disclosures often unfold over time, with announcements, prepared remarks, and discussion spanning multiple high-frequency return intervals. Financial NLP benchmarks can therefore suffer from a within-event timing mismatch when the prediction target begins before the textual or audio input used by a model could be complete. Chronological train--test splits do not prevent this mismatch, because it occurs inside individual events rather than across samples. We introduce an Availability Contract, which requires a benchmark to state the input boundary, evidence for input availability, the outcome start, and the claims supported by that evidence. We apply this framework to 552 earnings calls from 24 firms. For each call, we hold the return endpoint fixed and compare the previous close, a documentary call-start proxy, and a completion proxy based on reconstructed audio end plus a stipulated processing allowance. At this baseline, moving from the call-start proxy to the completion proxy flips return signs for 9.4% of calls. Holding completion-clock cutpoints fixed, 28.3% change quintile. In an independent release-session analysis of a public earnings-call volatility benchmark, shifting before-market target windows forward by one trading session raises three-day mean squared error by 18.1-21.4% across four frozen prediction streams, while their point rankings remain unchanged. Together, the results show that labels and losses can depend materially on the declared outcome clock even when model rankings appear stable. evidence.title: When Does "Post-Call" Begin? An Availability Contract for Earnings-Call NLP Benchmarks
evidence.abstract: Corporate financial disclosures often unfold over time, with announcements, prepared remarks, and discussion spanning multiple high-frequency return intervals. Financial NLP benchmarks can therefore suffer from a within-event timing mismatch when the prediction target begins before the textual or audio input used by a model could be complete. Chronological train--test splits do not prevent this mismatch, because it occurs inside individual events rather than across samples. We introduce an Availability Contract, which requires a benchmark to state the input boundary, evidence for input availability, the outcome start, and the claims supported by that evidence. We apply this framework to 552 earnings calls from 24 firms. For each call, we hold the return endpoint fixed and compare the previous close, a documentary call-start proxy, and a completion proxy based on reconstructed audio end plus a stipulated processing allowance. At this baseline, moving from the call-start proxy to the completion proxy flips return signs for 9.4% of calls. Holding completion-clock cutpoints fixed, 28.3% change quintile. In an independent release-session analysis of a public earnings-call volatility benchmark, shifting before-market target windows forward by one trading session raises three-day mean squared error by 18.1-21.4% across four frozen prediction streams, while their point rankings remain unchanged. Together, the results show that labels and losses can depend materially on the declared outcome clock even when model rankings appear stable. The Availability Contract makes this assumption explicit and ties post-input claims to the available timing evidence.

title: Peluang Technopreneurship Berbasis Generative AI dalam Pengembangan Bisnis Digital: Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) mengubah cara individu dan organisasi memproduksi konten, membangun produk, mengolah informasi, serta menetapkan keputusan bisnis. Perubahan ini memberi ruang baru bagi technopreneur untuk merintis dan mengembangkan bisnis digital dengan sumber daya yang lebih hemat. Penelitian ini memetakan peluang, manfaat, tantangan, dan arah pengembangan technopreneurship berbasis GenAI melalui Systematic Literature Review (SLR) yang berpedoman pada prinsip PRISMA. Publikasi yang dikaji mencakup artificial intelligence, generative AI, kewirausahaan, kewirausahaan digital, dan inovasi model bisnis. Hasil sintesis memperlihatkan bahwa GenAI dapat membantu menemukan peluang usaha, memperbarui model bisnis, menghasilkan konten, menyesuaikan layanan, menganalisis pasar, dan mendukung keputusan. Namun, penggunaannya menimbulkan persoalan ketergantungan teknologi, mutu keluaran, keamanan data, kekayaan intelektual, bias, serta kebutuhan akan kompetensi manusia. Temuan ini menegaskan bahwa nilai technopreneurship tidak bersumber dari penggunaan AI semata, melainkan dari perpaduannya dengan pengetahuan bidang, kreativitas, validasi manusia, dan tata kelola yang bertanggung jawab.

title: Adaptive Self-Reward and Mutual-Reward Switching in World Self-and-Mutual Models: A Framework for Autonomous Learning and Coordination
abstract: World models provide internal representations of environmental dynamics that support prediction, planning, and decision-making. However, the mechanisms through which a world-model-based system evaluates its own progress and coordinates evaluation across interacting models remain important design questions. Conventional individual reward mechanisms can support autonomous learning but may overlook opportunities for coordination, whereas shared or mutual reward mechanisms can encourage cooperation but may introduce communication costs, coordination overhead, and dependence on other models. This paper proposes an Adaptive Self-Reward and Mutual-Reward Switching framework for World Self-and-Mutual Models (ASRMS-WSMM). The framework integrates self-reward, mutual reward, and adaptive reward-mode selection into a world-model-level architecture rather than treating the system as a collection of large language models. The proposed architecture distinguishes self-model evaluation from cross-model evaluation and allows the system to operate in self-reward mode, mutual-reward mode, or a hybrid mode. A context-sensitive controller estimates individual learning progress, predictive uncertainty, cross-model contribution, coordination benefit, communication cost, and reward reliability. These signals inform the selection and weighting of reward modes over time. The framework also introduces a model-level reward attribution mechanism intended to distinguish improvements produced by an individual model from improvements associated with interactions among models. A formal objective, operational algorithm, evaluation protocol, and falsifiable hypotheses are presented. The paper does not claim empirical validation. Instead, it establishes a testable research framework for investigating whether adaptive reward-mode selection can improve learning efficiency, model quality, coordination, and resource utilization compared with fixed self-reward and fixed mutual-reward strategies.

title: Argus Financial Data Infrastructure for AI Agents and Human-Directed Trading
abstract: The long-term significance of AI lies in changing how cognitive capabilities are accumulated, accessed, and organized. Individuals learn within the limits of their time and experience, whereas model capabilities can draw on collective investments in research, computation, data, and feedback systems. This paper adopts an explicit forward-looking position: continually developing model-driven systems may achieve overall cognitive capabilities that exceed those of any individual human. This judgment forms the strategic design premise of Argus. Rapid model development also raises a product choice: how can financial research continually adopt a task-appropriate "brain" without tying established workflows to a fixed model? On this basis, the paper explains why Argus focuses on an independent data layer. LLMs provide understanding, reasoning, and planning capabilities; caller-side agents organize these capabilities into tasks; and Argus supplies financial facts together with their semantics, evidence, time information, and quality status. An independent data function allows callers to reevaluate and replace models while continuing to use the financial records they have accumulated. As models become more capable, sufficient, detailed, and verifiable real-world inputs become more valuable in putting those capabilities to use. The paper distinguishes parameter training, runtime retrieval, and workflow memory to explain how data supports tasks through different mechanisms. We further discuss a division of responsibilities in which humans and models jointly define objectives, agents conduct research continuously, and caller-side systems make trading judgments and take authorized actions. Individuals organizing research at the scale of a team, humans taking a greater role in setting objectives and providing oversight, and agents expanding their autonomy subject to verification requirements are the long-term directions proposed here. Future competition may increasingly depend on how participants combine models, data, tools, and boundaries. This is a position and design-argument paper that proposes testable propositions. It reports no new experiments on intelligence comparisons, model replacement costs, or trading returns; its original diagrams explain relationships rather than measured effects.

title: La Diferencia entre Simulación Estadística de Inteligencia y Heurística de Inteligencia Verdadera
abstract: Este documento analiza la diferencia estructural entre la inteligencia estadística de los modelos LLM y la inteligencia heurística verdadera basada en rutas conceptuales permanentes. Se explica cómo la heurística permite consultas O(1), memoria no redundante, navegación relacional, cálculo autónomo y representación real del conocimiento sin depender de Big Data ni entrenamiento masivo. El texto demuestra que la heurística es determinista, eficiente, transparente y escalable, y que transforma la computación en un sistema de lógica pura. Se incluyen ejemplos, código, análisis arquitectónico y una visión completa de cómo la heurística supera por diseño a los modelos probabilísticos.

title: Financial Implications of AI-Generated Video Production
abstract: This chapter examines the financial and managerial implications of AI-generated video production in digital marketing. Using a structured literature review and conceptual synthesis guided by TOE and DOI, it identifies cost savings, hidden ownership risks, and capability-dependent benefits. It proposes the AIVIE framework to evaluate ROI, adoption readiness, governance, marketing performance, investment sustainability, and long-term organizational value, providing managers and resource-constrained SMEs with a practical basis for informed AI investment and strategic decision-making over time.

title: Tackling LLM Hallucination with Abductive Reasoning
abstract: Large language models can produce convincing explanations that rely on invented facts, unsupported assumptions, or overlooked alternatives. This paper presents a method for checking whether such explanations are supported by the available evidence. The method identifies the assumptions needed to support a model's answer, checks for contradictions, and compares the answer with alternative explanations that require fewer unsupported assumptions. It also considers how an explanation is organized, distinguishing its central claims from supporting details and examining how statements support or challenge one another. Evaluation on four datasets shows that incorporating this structure improves the detection of hallucinated reasoning compared with the same detection approach without structural information. Additional experiments examine the contributions of explanation structure, assumption checking, and comparison with alternatives. The findings suggest that checking both the evidence behind an answer and the organization of its explanation can help detect and explain failures in language-model reasoning.

title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution
abstract: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights. The agent harness is iteratively optimized to achieve higher performance on the search set. But how much of this gain reflects benchmark-specific overfitting or additional inference-time compute, and how much may generalize beyond the search set? In this work, we introduce Harness-Delta Attribution (HDA), an evaluation protocol that dissects an evolution gain into artifact-driven overfitting, gains explained by test-time scaling, and the remainder, which gives an upper bound on residual generalizable improvement. We apply HDA to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks. In 21 of these settings that show statistically significant search-set gains, we find that a large share of the improvement is explained by overfitting or test-time scaling. Specifically, among these 21 settings, overfitting and test-time scaling account for 54% and 14% of the gain on average; their combined share exceeds 50% in 14 settings. The residual and held-out transfer vary substantially across tasks, models, and frameworks. Importantly, search-set gains often fail to transfer to held-out tasks, and provide limited evidence that they will persist under practical distribution shifts. Moreover, validation-based signals are insufficient to prevent overfitting. These results motivate attribution-aware evaluation in future harness evolution research.

title: MOSS: Mode-Oriented Source Shaping for Robot Flow Matching Policies
abstract: In robotic manipulation, the same observation often admits multiple feasible actions. Generative policies such as diffusion and flow matching naturally capture such multimodal behaviors, yet which mode is executed is left to random sampling and cannot be actively controlled. We propose Mode-Oriented Source Shaping (MOSS), which turns mode selection into an explicit choice of where generation starts. We first reveal, both empirically and theoretically, that deterministic flow transport induces mode-dependent structure in the source space. Under ideal deterministic ODE transport, distinct behavioral modes have distinct source-space preimages, while practical approximation errors can blur their boundaries due to imbalanced data, limited model capacity, and few inference steps. Motivated by this source-space structure, MOSS constructs semantically aligned mode-specific Gaussian sources that encode mode identity in the initial noise. A modality-strength estimator predicts the local degree of multimodality, which adaptively controls the geometry of the mode-specific sources. It contracts them toward a shared Gaussian where behaviors are similar and separates them near behavioral branching points. During deployment, the desired behavior is selected at inference simply by sampling from the corresponding component. Across 6 simulated and 3 real-world manipulation tasks, MOSS steers to the target mode up to 100% of the time with high task success, recovers minority modes at over 90% guidance rate under a 10:90 imbalance dataset, and surpasses mode-conditioned flow policy by 43.3 points of guidance rate on real robots.

title: Conditional Mean Flows: Few-Step Densities for Simulation-Based Inference
abstract: Flow matching has emerged as a powerful generative family for simulation-based inference (SBI). However, sampling and density evaluation require numerical integration at inference time. This makes posterior sampling in neural posterior estimation costly. More importantly, it can make repeated likelihood evaluation prohibitively expensive and impractical for Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling, which may require thousands of repeated density evaluations. Here, we develop conditional mean flows for posterior and likelihood approximation, combining few-step sampling with tractable density evaluation. We show that the mean flow objective identifies conditional flow maps and that independent masking enables direct estimation of marginal likelihoods. We evaluate both posterior and likelihood estimation across several tasks and show that conditional mean flows retain the flexibility of flow-based density estimators while significantly reducing inference time. In particular, single-step conditional mean flow density evaluation yields estimation error comparable to 200-step flow matching while enabling about 200-fold faster downstream MCMC sampling.

title: Matoi: Selective Revalidation of Consequence Evidence for Agent Authorization
abstract: Matoi separates reusable consequence evidence from current execution authority and durable occurrence history. Its finite query-aware contract covers branches, ordered collections and negative lookups. A consumer reuses only its own checked evidence whose observations remain valid; signed requests, live grants, quota and uncertain outcomes remain separate obligations. Conditional correctness arguments distinguish locally serialized claims from nontransactional remote effects. Two studies strengthen cost attribution and domain evaluation. A 1,440-cell matched-wire study repeats 144 authored inputs. With compact input bytes identical, reuse reduces complete lifecycle cost by 3.49 percent in JS and 1.79 percent in Python. Combined representation/reuse reductions against full proof are 10.87 and 16.53 percent; five of twelve family intervals for the matched comparison cross one in each language. A prospectively frozen AgentDojo Banking mapping covers 5/16 user plans and 7/9 attack plans. Both governed strategies preserve five exact benign transfers and refuse 35 reused attack-plan/policy crosses. Pre-satisfied utility predicates are reported separately from completed work. These are original scripted synthetic tools, not autonomous agents or a real bank. Earlier studies retain cheaper protected-cache alternatives, policy-compatible phishing, provider duplication and post-claim revocation. Separate JS/Python consumers establish finite-profile interoperability within the same project; durable recovery rechecks evidence and retains uncertain reservations. The results support a bounded, auditable reuse and execution contract, not a new general incremental algorithm, arbitrary-tool closure, atomic third-party commitment or production superiority.

title: Monotone Piecewise-Linear Harmonization of Multitemporal Multispectral Surface Reflectance With Unsupervised Deep Multiview Pseudoinvariant Features Learning
abstract: Surface reflectance products derived from optical satellite may exhibit systematic inconsistencies across acquisition dates, because atmospheric correction is generally performed independently for each image. Such residual biases distort the temporal behavior of invariant ground targets and reduce the reliability of multitemporal surface reflectance analysis. This study proposes Deep Multitemporal Generalized Canonical Correlation Analysis (DeepMGCCA), an unsupervised deep multiview pseudoinvariant feature learning framework that integrates Deep Generalized Canonical Correlation Analysis (GCCA) with Multivariate Alteration Detection (MAD) to identify deep-pseudoinvariant features (DIFs) for the removal of surface reflectance biases across multitemporal satellite observations. Unlike conventional MAD-based approaches that rely on linear GCCA, the proposed framework replaces date-specific linear projections with a shared convolutional encoder. The framework learns deep invariant features (DIFs) directly from pixel-weighted canonical variates via iterative reweighting strategy, while a reconstruction regularizer preserves surface reflectance information and prevents degenerate collapse from suppressing genuine temporal variability. Experiments were conducted on four annual Landsat-8/9 and Sentinel-2 acquisitions across four regions of interest (ROIs) to evaluate four DIF-based harmonization transforms. A monotone piecewise-linear transform derived from DIFs quantiles consistently achieved the largest bias reduction, lowering the between-date spectral angle by up to 2.54 and RMSE by 0.015, and raising PSNR by up to 4.04~dB. evidence.title: Monotone Piecewise-Linear Harmonization of Multitemporal Multispectral Surface Reflectance With Unsupervised Deep Multiview Pseudoinvariant Features Learning
evidence.abstract: Surface reflectance products derived from optical satellite may exhibit systematic inconsistencies across acquisition dates, because atmospheric correction is generally performed independently for each image. Such residual biases distort the temporal behavior of invariant ground targets and reduce the reliability of multitemporal surface reflectance analysis. This study proposes Deep Multitemporal Generalized Canonical Correlation Analysis (DeepMGCCA), an unsupervised deep multiview pseudoinvariant feature learning framework that integrates Deep Generalized Canonical Correlation Analysis (GCCA) with Multivariate Alteration Detection (MAD) to identify deep-pseudoinvariant features (DIFs) for the removal of surface reflectance biases across multitemporal satellite observations. Unlike conventional MAD-based approaches that rely on linear GCCA, the proposed framework replaces date-specific linear projections with a shared convolutional encoder. The framework learns deep invariant features (DIFs) directly from pixel-weighted canonical variates via iterative reweighting strategy, while a reconstruction regularizer preserves surface reflectance information and prevents degenerate collapse from suppressing genuine temporal variability. Experiments were conducted on four annual Landsat-8/9 and Sentinel-2 acquisitions across four regions of interest (ROIs) to evaluate four DIF-based harmonization transforms. A monotone piecewise-linear transform derived from DIFs quantiles consistently achieved the largest bias reduction, lowering the between-date spectral angle by up to 2.54 and RMSE by 0.015, and raising PSNR by up to 4.04~dB. These findings demonstrate the potential of deep invariant feature learning for multitemporal surface reflectance bias removal while highlighting the importance of preserving physically meaningful temporal and spectral information during nonlinear representation learning.

title: Perbandingan Metode Mean Shift Clustering Dan Density Peaks Clustering Dalam Pengelompokan Provinsi Berdasarkan Indikator Kesehatan Lingkungan Di Indonesia
abstract: Kesehatan lingkungan merupakan salah satu aspek penting dalam meningkatkan kualitas hidup masyarakat. Namun, capaian indikator kesehatan lingkungan masih menunjukkan perbedaan antarprovinsi di Indonesia sehingga diperlukan analisis pengelompokan untuk mengidentiikasi provinsi yang memiliki karakteristik serupa. Penelitian ini bertujuan membandingkan kinerja metode Mean Shift Clustering dan Density Peaks Clustering (DPC) dalam mengelompokkan provinsi berdasarkan indikator kesehatan lingkungan di Indonesia. Data yang digunakan merupakan data sekunder Profil Kesehatan Indonesia Tahun 2024 yang mencakup 38 provinsi dengan sembilan indikator kesehatan lingkungan. Analisis dilakukan menggunakan bahasa pemrograman Python. Penentuan parameter bandwidth pada Mean Shift Clustering menggunakan pendekatan quantile, sedangkan parameter cut‑off distance pada DPC menggunakan pendekatan persentil. Kinerja kedua metode dievaluasi menggunakan Silhouette Coeficient (SC) dan Davies‑Bouldin Index (DBI). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Mean Shift Clustering menghasilkan dua klaster, sedangkan DPC menghasilkan dua klaster utama dan satu klaster outlier yang merepresentasikan provinsi dengan karakteristik berbeda dari klaster lainnya. DPC memperoleh nilai SC sebesar 0,7257 dan DBI sebesar 0,3342, sedangkan Mean Shift Clustering memperoleh nilai SC sebesar 0,7010 dan DBI sebesar 0,4440. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa DPC menghasilkan struktur klaster yang lebih kompak dan memiliki pemisahan antarklaster yang lebih baik, sehingga lebih sesuai digunakan untuk pengelompokan provinsi berdasarkan indikator kesehatan lingkungan di Indonesia.

title: Monitoring Explanation Drift in Longitudinal NLP Pipelines: A Cross-Domain Study under Temporal Distribution Shift
abstract: This paper studies explanation drift : the temporal instability of ranked human-readable terms produced by fixed explanation mechanisms in longitudinal NLP pipelines. We compare corpus-level TF–IDF explanations with model-level explanations derived from logistic-regression coefficients in arXiv and PubMed abstracts from 2014 to 2024. The vocabulary is learned only from the 2014–2016 reference window and then frozen, approximating a deployed monitoring scenario. arXiv is used as the primary supervised setting, while PubMed provides a cross-domain robustness check with query-defined weak labels. Results show that model-level explanations drift more than corpus-level TF–IDF summaries. On arXiv, mean DriftScore is 0.50 for model-level explanations and 0.15 for TF–IDF, a 3.33-fold increase with strong statistical support (padj = 0.0040). On PubMed, the same direction appears with smaller magnitude, 0.20 versus 0.13, but is not significant after Bonferroni correction (padj = 0.0938). The proposed audit rule produces no automatic alerts under the strict configuration because observed drift does not strictly exceed the null 95th percentile, illustrating the distinction between measurable explanation turnover and drift that is sufficiently unusual to trigger operational review.
